drills.title: Protected names get no short alias
hints: Define Foo.bar : Nat as 1, marked so that opening Foo will not create the short alias bar.
Open the namespace Foo.
Check bar, wrapped in a #guard_msgs whose expected message is the error: Unknown identifier `bar`.
Check the full name Foo.bar.

drills.title: Locally enabling a list-ordering instance
hints: Define instLe, an abbreviation of type LE (List α), built as a structure instance whose le field is isPrefix.
Open an anonymous section.
Inside it, use the attribute command to make instLe an instance with local scope.
Anonymous example: for as : List α, prove as ≤ as, in term mode, by building the pair of the witness [] and a proof by the simp tactic directly.
Close the section.

Repeat the same example after the section, wrapped in a #guard_msgs expecting the error that Lean failed to synthesize an instance of LE (List α), followed by its hint suggesting set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true.

drills.title: Turning on verbose pretty-printing
hints: Turn on the options pp.explicit and pp.universes, and turn off pp.notation.
Check the type of the proposition 2 + 2 = 4.
Reduce the equation between the function adding 2 to its argument x and the function adding 3 to x.
Check the type of the function adding 1 to its argument x, applied to 1.

drills.title: Inspecting the product type's operations
hints: Check the types, with all implicit arguments made explicit, of Prod's constructor mk, its projections fst and snd, and its recursor rec.

drills.title: Naming arguments to folds and substitutions
hints: Define sum of xs : List Nat by a left fold over xs (called as a method on xs), passing the initial value 0 by its parameter name init, and passing addition written in the centered-dot placeholder shorthand.
Evaluate sum on [1, 2, 3, 4].
Anonymous example with implicit naturals a, b and implicit predicate p : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop, hypotheses h₁ : p a b b and h₂ : b = a, proving p a a b.
Term-mode proof: Eq.subst applied to h₂ and h₁, supplying its motive by parameter name as a lambda over x giving p a x b.

drills.title: Extracting binder parts from terms
hints: Inductive type Term with four constructors whose arguments are named: var with name : String; num with val : Nat; app with fn : Term and arg : Term; lambda with name : String, type : Term, and body : Term.

Define getBinderName : Term → Option String by equations: on a lambda, bind just its name argument (by parameter name) to n, eliding all remaining explicit arguments, and return some n; on anything else, return none.
Define getBinderType : Term → Option Term the same way, binding the lambda's type argument to t.
